sentences.text: Shri Atul Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Mohit Shivhare - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St
Shri Chandra Prakash Sharma/complainant is present in person before this court.

Heard on Ia No.16860/2024, first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. moved on behalf of
appellant Hitendra Mudgal seeking suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.

Appellant stood convicted under Section 420 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo four years'
rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 467 of the IPC to undergo five years'
rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- and under Section 468 of the IPC to undergo four years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 20.07.2024 passed by First Additional Sessions Judge,
Sabalgarh, District Morena in S.T. No.411/2015.

entities.text:
First Additional Sessions Judge,
Sabalgarh, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant Hitendra Mudgal contends that it is a case of agreement of sale,
the document in question (Annexure P/8) was cancellation of earlier agreement.
After cancellation of the agreement, the amount received in furtherence of earlier agreement to sale was returned.
Therefore, no wrongful loss was caused to the complainant.

Learned counsel further referring to the evidence of Diwakar Sharma (PW-13)
submits that Diwakar Sharma did not support the prosecution, rather the evidence of Diwakar Sharma substantiated the defence of appellant/accused.
Civil dispute is given color of criminal prosecution.
Learned Trial Court did not consider the evidence on record in proper perspective.
Learned Counsel further submits that impugned judgment passed by learned Trial Court is based on assumption, conjectures and surmises.
The learned Trial Court has committed an error in convicting and sentencing the present appellant without appreciating the prosecution evidence properly.
No criminal antecedent is alleged against the appellant.

There is no likelihood of early hearing of appeal Hitendra Mudgal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51812374/
1 in near future.

sentences.text: On these grounds, learned counsel prays that execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended and he may be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned Counsel for respondent-State assisted by the complainant opposes the application and prays for its rejection and submits that forged document in question (Ex.P/8) is proved beyond doubt by the evidence of hand writing expert.

Further, the evidence on record clearly makes out forgery of document in question as Diwakar Sharma executor of the document was not present at the time of execution but the document bears his signature.
The appellant was beneficiary of the transaction, therefore, trial court committed no error in convicting the appellant for the offences punishable under sections 420, 467 and 468 of the IPC.

In view of the direct evidence available on record, impugned judgment does not suffer from any illegality and factual infirmity,
therefore, appellant does not 3 CRA-8848-2024 deserve to be released on bail.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Upon hearing the learned Counsel for the parties but without commenting upon rival contentions, touching merits of the evidence on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, appellant does not deserve suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.
Consequently, I.A. No.16860/2024 stands dismissed.
